 Non Inverting Amplifier Gain: Av = 1 + Rf/R1 Formula, Derivation, Input Impedance, Voltage Follower Case, Bandwidth and Resistor Selection With Solved Examples

 The non inverting op amp stage boosts a small sensor signal without flipping its polarity or loading the source. Here you will learn its gain equation, its limits and how to pick resistors that work on a real board.

 
 Av = 1 + Rf/R1 
 Derivation 
 Input Impedance 
 Bandwidth 
 Calculator 
 




 The gain of a non inverting op amp stage depends only on two resistors and is always one or more. This guide covers the formula, its derivation, the follower case, bandwidth and practical resistor choice with solved examples.


 
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn non inverting amplifier gain, from the simple 1 + Rf/R1 formula to bandwidth and resistor selection for real instrument circuits.


 
 
 
 What Is Non Inverting Amplifier Gain?

 Non inverting amplifier gain is the ratio of output voltage to input voltage of an op amp stage where the signal enters the plus input, and it equals Av = 1 + Rf/R1. The output stays in phase with the input, and the gain can never fall below one.

 
Av = Vout ÷ Vin
 Av = 1 + Rf ÷ R1 
Gain in dB = 20 × log10(Av)
Rf = feedback resistor, R1 = resistor to ground


 The circuit is the twin of the stage described in our inverting amplifier gain formula article, with the input and ground swapped. If you are new to op amps, start with op amp basics to learn the two golden rules used below.

 
 
 Image credit: Utah State University . Diagram courtesy of the Utah State University Engineering Tutoring Center, shown here for educational reference. 
 
 In the lower circuit the input goes straight to the plus pin, while Rf and R1 form a divider from the output back to the minus pin. That divider is the whole secret of the gain.

 Do You Know?
 Analog Devices notes that a precision op amp can have an open loop DC gain of about 160 dB, or 100 million. Negative feedback trades almost all of that for a stable gain set only by resistors.

 Non Inverting Amplifier Formula Derivation

 With negative feedback, the op amp drives its output until both inputs sit at nearly the same voltage, so the minus pin also equals Vin. No current flows into the inputs, so Rf and R1 carry the same current.

 
V minus pin = Vout × R1 ÷ (R1 + Rf)
V minus pin = Vin (virtual short)
Vout ÷ Vin = (R1 + Rf) ÷ R1
 Av = 1 + Rf ÷ R1 


 The first line is just the voltage divider rule applied to the feedback network. Because the divider ratio is always less than one, the gain is always at least one, which is why this stage cannot attenuate.

 Key Points
 Av = 1 + Rf/R1, always 1 or more
 Output is in phase with the input
 Input impedance is very high, close to that of the op amp itself
 Bandwidth ≈ GBW ÷ noise gain, and noise gain equals signal gain here
 Rf = 0 or R1 open gives a voltage follower with g
